description.narrative:
Full Project Title: Increasing the access of women victims of sexual violence to services for advocating derivative regulations from the Sexual Violence Criminal Act
This program is entitled increasing the access of women victims of sexual violence toservices toadvocate for regulations derived from the TPKS Law. The aim is to advocate for regulations derived from the TPKS Law, especially those relating to integrated services for handling cases of sexual violence.
The strategies used are (1) strengthening access to casehandling services for victims of sexual violence in 3 areas (Aceh, Central Java and NTT). With the diversity and vulnerability of victims of sexual violence such as in Central Java with the vulnerability of victims from sexual minority groups / LBT (Lesbian Bisexual and Transsexual), in Aceh with a specific area that applies Islamic Shari'ah and NTT with the peculiarities of customary and religious areas; this assistance to access medical, legal, psychological and social services. Strengthening access to services including support group services which include counselling activities including group counselling, therapy, case discussions, discussions about the rights of women victims. (2) Strengthening the network of civil society organizations in handling cases of sexual violence through strengthening the understanding of civil society networks and service institutions regarding the TPKS Law and strengthening the documentation of experiences in handling cases of sexual violence. Theresults of this documentation are used for advocacy for PP on Integrated Services and (3) strengthening the state's commitment to the protection of women victims of sexual violence through meetings with ministries/agencies and lobbying series to discuss government regulations on integrated services.
The expected result of this program is increased access to services for victims of sexual violence as indicated by (1) 150 women victims of sexual violence who received assistance in accessing services, (2) 60 women victims of sexual violence received recovery services through a support group mechanism, (3 ) increasing knowledge of civil society organizations and service institutions about the TPKS Law (4) There are documented results of handling cases of sexual violence in 3 regions (Aceh, Central Java and NTT), (5) There are derivative regulations of the TPKS Law on Integrated Services
Goals: Increased Access to Services for Women Victims of Sexual Violence through the Implementation of the TPKS Law
Objectives: 1. Strengthening access to services for women victims of sexual violence in Central Java, Aceh and NTT 2. Strengthening civil society networks and service providers in handling cases of sexual violence 3. Encouraging theratification of PPand Presidential Regulations derived from the TPKS Law on UPTD PPA and Procedures for the Prevention and Handlingof Sexual Violence Cases

participating-org.narrative:
VISION: Strengthening access and control of vulnerable and marginalized poor women over legal and human rights resources for the realization of gender justice which will be achieved through Mission: 1. Strengthening access of marginally vulnerable poorwomen to legal aid that is gender-just. 2. Develop knowledge management to promote women's human rights. 3. Strengthening the women's movement as a movement for social change. 4. Strengthen organizational accountability, management and governance
LRC-KJHAM is a non-governmental organization based in Palebon Pedurungan, Semarang, Central Java. The LRC KJHAM began as a women's rights working group in Central Java. The Working Group for Gender Justice and Human Rights (K3JHAM) was founded by LBH Semarang-LBH Indonesia Foundation on July 24, 1999. K3JHAM was founded on 'Anti-Violence Against Women Day' Novib's YLBHI program funds K3JHAM.K3JHAM pioneered the '16 Day Campaign against Violence Against Women' in 2000. Komnas Perempuan coordinated this national program. K3JHAM defends women's rights in court and in public and counsels violence victims. K3JHAM works to improve the gender justice and responsiveness of construction legal aid (BHS) for LBH offices.YLBHI deemed K3JHAM's work complete in 2002. LBHSemarang saw the importance of K3JHAM, so it formed LRC KJHAM under the Secretariat Foundation for Gender Justice and Human Rights (Sukma Foundation). New people are activated in the LRC KJHAM Working Group (K3JHAM). Their experience with international human rights legal instruments, such as preparing the Report onAlternative Implementation of CEDAW, advocating for Beijing+5 in the UN General Assembly (2000), and developing Feminist Participatory Action Research (FPAR) and Woman's Rights Impact Assessment (WRIA), strengthens institutional work. LRC-KJHAM and global networks. GAATW Bangkok and TdH Jakarta supported FPAR's development.
